firmware.details.what: Report everything known about one build: where it is, what it is, and what has been decided about it.

params.name: version
params.what: the build's version or imported label

params.name: role
params.what: which role, when one label carries more than one

params.name: board
params.what: which board; absent means a build for this machine

firmware.details.answers: Answered from the library, so a published build nobody has fetched is described too: `on_disk` is then false and `path` and `bytes` are empty. `in_use` counts the nodes pinned to it, `kind`, `bootable` and `flash_mb` are read from a board image and say nothing about a native build, `settings_path` is where its settings would be written whether any exist or not, and `modified` is absent for a build not on this machine. A label naming more than one build is refused rather than guessed at.

example.what: find out where a build lives and what is running it

firmware.update.what: Rename a build, move it to another board or role, or change how it is run.

params.name: version
params.what: the build to change, by its current version or label

params.name: role
params.what: its current role, when one label carries more than one

params.name: label
params.what: rename it to this; unchanged when absent

params.name: new_role
params.what: run it as this role instead; unchanged when absent

params.name: new_board
params.what: move it to this board instead; unchanged when absent

params.name: card_required
params.what: this firmware will not get far without storage in the board's slot, so every node running it is given a card whatever it would otherwise have had

params.name: coproc_at_reset
params.what: start this build's coprocessors enabled, which the part does not do - for a firmware that traps inside its own exception vector and cannot be seen past

params.name: notes
params.what: what the next person should know about this build

firmware.update.answers: The build's identity after the change comes back, with `renamed` saying whether the file actually moved and `repinned` how many nodes were pointed at the new name, which happens on their behalf so none is left naming a build nothing answers to. `settings` holds `coproc_at_reset`, `card_required` and `notes` as they now stand. Refused for a build not on this machine, and refused while a node is running it.

params.notes: the arm this study compares against

example.what: record what the next person should know about a build
